title: Chart Watch: Stella Lefty, Yung Miami, and Malcolm Todd Eye Top 10 Breakthroughs
summary: The Billboard Hot 100's upper ranks may seem static, with Ella Langley's 'Choosin' Texas' notching a 12th nonconsecutive week at No. 1, but just outside the top 10, a trio of tracks is gaining momentum—and they could soon disrupt the chart's hierarchy. At No. 13, Stella Lefty's 'Boston' reaches a new peak. The country-pop earworm cleverly interpolates the melody from Noah Kahan's 'Stick Season' (Kahan even gets a writing credit), but Lefty transforms it into a buoyant, windows-down summer anthem. Given how word-of-mouth country hits have legs—just look at Langley—'Boston' could be a slow-burn contender. Further down, Yung Miami lands her highest-charting solo hit yet with 'Spend Dat' at No. 19. The rapper, known for her work with City Girls and a 2023 collab that peaked at No. 69, has now cracked the top 20 for the first time on her own. The viral track signals a potential solo breakout. Meanwhile, singer-songwriter and TikTok favorite Malcolm Todd hits No. 22 with 'Earrings,' a 2024 track that's become his biggest hit. Todd's new album, Do That Again, recently debuted in the top five, suggesting his streaming fanbase is converting to chart success. On the albums side, K-pop powerhouse ATEEZ debuts at No. 1 with Golden Hour: Part.5, moving 223,000 units—mostly physical sales, fueled by 30 CD variants and five vinyl editions. They dethrone Olivia Rodrigo's you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love, which slips to No. 2. ATEEZ now holds the record for most top 10 albums by a group in the 2020s, surpassing Stray Kids and Tomorrow X Together. With summer in full swing, these rising acts could soon challenge Langley's reign—and Taylor Swift's 'I Knew It, I Knew You' at No. 2 might also get a boost from her recent wedding buzz.
why_it_matters: These chart movements reveal how streaming and viral moments are reshaping the path to the top 10, giving genre-blending newcomers like Stella Lefty and Malcolm Todd a shot. At the same time, K-pop's physical-sale power shows that dedicated fan armies can still dominate weekly rankings, reflecting a truly global music market.

background_read: The Billboard Hot 100, the music industry's main singles chart, often sees slower movement in summer as radio playlists solidify; new tracks can slowly climb based on streaming momentum.
Ella Langley (a breakout country artist from Alabama) has held No. 1 for months with 'Choosin' Texas,' a song about rural pride that resonated widely on TikTok.

Interpolation — when a new song borrows a melody or lyric from an older track — is common in pop; Noah Kahan (whose folk ballad 'Stick Season' went viral in 2022) is now credited on 'Boston' for its use of his melody.
Yung Miami (real name Caresha Brownlee, of the rap duo City Girls) previously charted as a featured guest, but 'Spend Dat' marks her solo breakthrough.
K-pop acts like ATEEZ (a South Korean octet formed by KQ Entertainment) often release multiple collectible CD versions, boosting physical sales for a strong first-week chart debut.
Article_Structure: LEAD: Hot 100's top 10 looks static, but three tracks are rising just outside.
└─ Contrast: Ella Langley's 'Choosin' Texas' sits at No. 1 for a 12th nonconsecutive week.
├─ Stella Lefty's 'Boston' at No.13: interpolates Noah Kahan's 'Stick Season,' transforms it into a summer anthem; described as a slow-burn contender.
├─ Yung Miami's 'Spend Dat' at No.19: first solo top-20 hit, signaling potential breakout beyond her City Girls fame.
└─ Malcolm Todd's 'Earrings' at No.22: backed by Top 5 album 'Do That Again,' converting streaming fanbase into chart success.
ALBUMS: ATEEZ's 'Golden Hour: Part.5' debuts at No.1 with 223,000 units, mostly from 30 CD variants and five vinyl editions.
└─ Milestone: ATEEZ now holds the record for most top 10 albums by a group in the 2020s, passing Stray Kids and Tomorrow X Together.
EXTRA CONTEXT: The album dethrones Olivia Rodrigo; Taylor Swift's wedding buzz could give her current single an extra push as summer unfolds.

perspectives.description: Rising artists such as Stella Lefty and Yung Miami benefit from organic, word-of-mouth buzz and clever sampling, which can fast-track them to mainstream success without major label machinery. Their breakthroughs show that the Hot 100 still has room for fresh sounds.

The chart's static top and reliance on physical variants raise concerns that numbers can be inflated through gimmicks like multiple CD editions. Some fear this overshadows fair competition and creates an uneven playing field for artists who can't afford such tactics.

Historically, summer tends to freeze the upper reaches of the Hot 100 as radio sticks to proven hits, while newer songs climb slowly via streaming and viral moments. This pattern helps explain why Ella Langley's reign has been so long and why these challengers haven't yet cracked the top 10.

If these tracks continue to gain momentum, the top 10 could soon see a shake-up that signals a broader shift in what types of songs—country-pop fusions, solo rap hits, indie-pop—can break through on radio. Labels may double down on slow-burn promotion strategies rather than front-loaded releases.
